subject: Meteorology
title: The Rain Gauge
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Rain Gauge.

hook.text: Rain gauges are among the simplest and oldest weather instruments—yet measuring rain accurately is surprisingly tricky.

buildup.text: Korean King Sejong standardized rain measurement in 1441—ordering gauges installed across the kingdom for crop planning.

discovery.text: Wind distorts catch—turbulence around the gauge causes undercatch, so exposed gauges miss 5–20% of actual rainfall.

twist.text: Tipping-bucket gauges automate counting—each tip records 0.2 mm of rain, but they miss heavy bursts between tips.

climax.text: Even today, rain gauge networks are sparse over oceans and remote areas—satellite estimates fill the global gaps.

punchline.text: A simple funnel and cylinder—still essential, still imperfect.

quiz.question: What problem affects rain gauge accuracy?
options: Wind-caused undercatch from turbulence around the gauge
